extracted.intended_audience: federal policymakers, Indian agents, commissioners, and legal practitioners responsible for implementing Indian treaties and land dispositions
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural, financial, and legal requirements for ratifying and carrying into effect the agreement with the Ute tribes: surveying, allotting, patenting, trust-fund creation, payments, commissions, reporting, and protections/conditions on allotted lands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Private cash entry tract limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to private entry, for cash in tracts not exceeding one quarter section by one purchaser.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taxation after first installment and tax-sale cure
rubrics_metrics.description: After the payment of the first installment ... such lands shall be subject to taxation according to the laws of the State of Kansas; Provided, That no sale of any such lands for taxes shall operate to deprive the United States of said lands, or any part of the purchase-price thereof, but if default be made in any installment ... such tax sale purchaser ... may, upon the day fixed for the public sale, and after such default has become final ... pay so much of said purchase-price as may remain unpaid, and shall thereupon be entitled to receive a patent for the same ... And provided further, That nothing in this act shall be so construed as to deprive or impair the right of the settler, of the right of redemption under the revenue laws of the State of Kansas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tax sale does not extinguish U.S. interest; tax purchaser may cure purchaser default by paying remaining purchase-price on public sale day; settler retains state-law redemption rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Register and receiver fees; proceeds to Indian fund
rubrics_metrics.description: The register and the receiver shall be allowed the same fees and commissions as are allowed by law for the disposal of the public lands, and the net proceeds of the sales and disposals, after deducting the expenses of such disposals, shall be deposited to the credit of the proper Indian fund, as provided by existing laws; and the Secretary of the Interior shall make all rules and regulations necessary to carry into effect the provisions of this act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Officials receive standard public-lands fees; net proceeds (less expenses) go to the designated Indian fund; Secretary to prescribe implementing rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Town-site law noninterference and claim requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in this act shall be construed to interfere in any manner with the operation of the town-site laws as applicable to those lands: Provided, That all claims for entry under said statutes shall be proved up and fully paid for, before the day fixed for the commencement of the public sales provided for in section three of this act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Town-site rights preserved; town-site claimants must have completed proof and full payment prior to public-sale date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interest on deferred purchase money
rubrics_metrics.description: In all cases arising under this act interest at the rate of five per cent, per annum shall be computed and paid upon all that part of the purchase money in respect to which time is given for the payment of the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 5% per annum interest applies to purchase-money installments where time is extended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ratification condition: amendment and payment proviso for White River Utes
rubrics_metrics.description: The agreement is accepted, ratified, and confirmed; amended by adding provisos that the proportion of money coming to the White River Utes shall not be paid until surrender/apprehension of guilty parties or until President is satisfied they are no longer living or have fled beyond U.S. limits; and appropriations for education and specified annuity payments added.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain payments to White River Utes are conditional on surrender/apprehension of implicated persons; President has discretion to appropriate up to $10,000 for education of selected youths; specified individual annuities for named persons for twenty years if living.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ratification quorum and consent requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Three-fourths of the adult male members of said confederated bands shall agree to and sign said agreement, upon presentation of the same to them, in open council.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agreement's effectiveness contingent on ratification by 75% of adult male tribal members in open council and subsequent certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agreement not to compel removal
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in this act contained, or in the agreement herein set forth, or in the amendments herein proposed to said agreement, shall be so construed as to compel any Ute Indian to remove from any lands that he or she claims in severalty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individuals claiming lands in severalty are not to be forced to remove.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chiefs' promise to surrender or aid apprehension
rubrics_metrics.description: The chiefs and headmen ... hereby promise and agree to procure the surrender to the United States, for trial and punishment, if found guilty, of those members ... implicated in the murder ... and ... that they will not in any manner obstruct, but faithfully aid, any officers of the United States ... to apprehend such presumably guilty parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tribal leadership obligated to assist in law-enforcement actions regarding named crimes and persons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designated settlement locations for bands
rubrics_metrics.description: The Southern Utes agree to remove to and settle upon the unoccupied agricultural lands on the La Plata River ... Uncompahgre Utes ... agricultural lands on Grand River ... The White River Utes agree to remove to and settle upon agricultural lands on the Uintah Reservation in Utah.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific relocation sites are prescribed; fallback to alternative unoccupied agricultural lands in nearby territories if insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allotments in severalty: sizes and grazing adjuncts
rubrics_metrics.description: Allotments in severalty of said lands shall be made as follows: To each head of a family one-quarter of a section, with an additional quantity of grazing land not exceeding one-quarter of a section. To each single person over eighteen years of age one-eighth of a section, with an additional quantity of grazing land not exceeding one-eighth of a section. To each orphan child under eighteen years of age one-eighth of a section, with an additional quantity of grazing land not exceeding one-eighth of a section; and to each other person, under eighteen years, now living, or who may be born prior to said allotments, one-eighth of a section, with a like quantity of grazing land.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allotment sizes are explicitly tiered by status (head of family, single adult, orphan/minor born prior to allotment); grazing land allowance equals the allotment but capped as stated; allocations made with commission advice and by selections of Indians/agents as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allotment selection rules and guardianship selection
rubrics_metrics.description: All allotments to be made with the advice of the commission hereinafter provided, upon the selection of the Indians, heads of families selecting for their minor children, and the agents making the allotment for each orphan child.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection process: adult Indians choose their allotments; heads choose for their minors; agents choose for orphans; commission advises and supervises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Noninterference with travel on highways
rubrics_metrics.description: The said chiefs and headmen ... further promise that they will not obstruct or in anywise interfere with travel upon any of the highways now open or hereafter to be opened by lawful authority in or upon any of the lands to be set apart for their use by virtue of this agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Freedom of travel across reserved/allotted lands to be maintained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent conditions: inalienability and tax exemption period
rubrics_metrics.description: The Government ... cause the lands so set apart to be properly surveyed and to be divided among the said Indians in severalty ... and to issue patents in fee simple to them respectively therefor, so soon as the necessary laws are passed by Congress. The title to be acquired by the Indians shall not be subject to alienation, lease, or incumbrance ... or subject to taxation of any character, but shall be and remain inalienable and not subject to taxation for the period of twenty-five years, and until such time thereafter as the President ... may see fit to remove the restriction, which shall be incorporated in the patents when issued, and any contract made prior to the removal of such restriction shall be void.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patents to include a 25-year restriction on alienation, incumbrance, and taxation; only the President may later remove restriction; contracts made before removal are void.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution of annuities and provisioning for removal
rubrics_metrics.description: So soon as the consent ... the President ... shall cause to be distributed among them in cash the sum of sixty thousand dollars of annuities now due and provided for, and so much more as Congress may appropriate for that purpose; and that a commission shall be sent to superintend the removal and settlement of the Utes, and to see that they are well provided with agricultural and pastoral lands sufficient for their future support, and upon such settlement being duly effected, that they are furnished with houses, wagons, agricultural implements, and stock cattle sufficient for their reasonable wants, and also such saw and grist mills as may be necessary ... and that the money ... shall be apportioned among the different bands ... One-third to La Plata, one-half to Grand River, and one-sixth to Uintah.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immediate cash annuity payment and appropriation for removal/settlement support; commissions to provide goods, structures, and apportion funds per band percentages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perpetual trust to yield $50,000 annually
rubrics_metrics.description: In consideration of the cession ... the United States, in addition to the annuities ... agrees to set apart and hold, as a perpetual trust for the said Ute Indians, a sum of money, or its equivalent in bonds of the United States, which shall be sufficient to produce the sum of fifty thousand dollars per annum, which sum of fifty thousand dollars shall be distributed per capita to them annually forever.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capital sum/bonds to be set aside as perpetual trust producing $50,000/year to be paid per capita forever.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency establishment, schools and education provision
rubrics_metrics.description: As soon as the President ... the agencies for the Uncompahgres and Southern Utes be removed to and established at suitable points ... and to aid in the support of the said Utes until such time as they shall be able to support themselves, and that in the mean time the United States Government will establish and maintain schools in the settlements of the Utes, and make all necessary provision for the education of their children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federal responsibility to establish agencies, provide interim support, and maintain schools to educate Ute children.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reaffirmation of prior treaty trust ($25,000/year)
rubrics_metrics.description: All provisions of the treaty of March second, eighteen hundred and sixty-eight, and the act of Congress approved April twenty-ninth, eighteen hundred and seventy-four, not altered by this agreement, shall continue in force, and the following words ... 'The United States agrees to set apart and hold, as a perpetual trust for the Ute Indians, a sum of money ... sufficient to produce the sum of twenty-five thousand dollars per annum ...' are hereby expressly reaffirmed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Existing trust obligations (producing $25,000/year) under prior treaties remain in force unless altered by this agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioners to appraise improvements and consider labor
rubrics_metrics.description: The commissioners above mentioned shall ascertain what improvements have been made by any member or members of the Ute Nation upon any part of the reservation in Colorado to be ceded to the United States ... and that payment in cash shall be made to the individuals having made and owning such improvements, upon a fair and liberal valuation of the same by the said commission, taking into consideration the labor bestowed upon the land.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission must value improvements generously and account for labor invested when paying owners in cash.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioners' appointment, pay, clerk, and bond
rubrics_metrics.description: The President ... authorized and empowered to appoint ... five commissioners, who shall receive compensation ... at the rate of ten dollars per diem while actually engaged, in addition to their actual traveling and other necessary expenses; and said commissioners shall have a clerk, at a salary of two hundred dollars per month, ... and who shall give bond in an amount to be fixed by the Secretary of the Interior, and shall act also as disbursing-officer for said commissioners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commissioners are presidential appointees with $10/day plus expenses; clerk paid $200/month must post bond and serve as disbursing officer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioners' duties: census, allotment, mapping, reporting, supervision
rubrics_metrics.description: Said commissioners shall, under such instructions ... present said agreement ...; appraise the improvements ...; take a careful census ... separating them under said census as follows: First Southern Utes, Second Uncompahgre Utes, Third White River Utes; show separately name of each head of family, numbers in family, distinguishing those over eighteen years from those under eighteen; show orphans separately; make accurate register of names, ages, occupations, and general condition, specifying those incompetent by reason of orphanage, minority, or other disability; select lands and allot them in severalty; superintend removal, location, and settlement; make a full report with name of each person allotted lands, condition, quantity, metes and bounds; make an accurate map of whole survey and partition; file copies in Dept. offices; report total acres allotted, amount tillable without irrigation, amount irrigation required and probable cost; locate agencies; furnish estimates of houses, school-houses, teachers, number of school-age children; exercise direct supervision and control of expenditures under this act while in the Ute country; render full and detailed account with vouchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission's responsibilities are comprehensive: demographic census, detailed records, land selection/allotment, mapping, appraisal, infrastructure estimates, fiscal supervision, and formal reporting with maps and vouchers to the Secretary of the Interior and land offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Survey, allotment completion and patent issuance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary of the Interior ... authorized to cause to be surveyed ... a sufficient quantity of land ... upon completion of said survey and enumeration ... the said commissioners shall cause allotments ... and whenever the report and proceedings of said commissioners ... are approved by the President ... he shall cause patents to issue to each and every allottee for the lands so allotted, with the same conditions, restrictions, and limitations mentioned therein as are provided in said agreement; and all the lands not so allotted ... shall be held and deemed to be public lands of the United States and subject to disposal under the laws providing for the disposal of the public lands, at the same price and on the same terms as other lands of like character, except as provided in this act: Provided, That none of said lands ... shall be liable to entry and settlement under the provisions of the homestead law; but shall be subject to cash entry only in accordance with existing law ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surveys and allotments must be completed and reported to the President for patent issuance; unallotted lands revert to public-land status but are not homestead-eligible and are sold for cash under law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority application of sale proceeds and sale procedures for improved subdivisions
rubrics_metrics.description: When sold the proceeds of said sale shall be first sacredly applied to reimbursing the United States for all sums paid out or set apart under this act by the government for the benefit of said Indians, and then, to be applied in payment for the lands at one dollar and twenty-five cents per acre which may be ceded to them by the United States outside of their reservation, in pursuance of this agreement. And the remainder, if any, shall be deposited in the Treasury as now provided by law for the benefit of the said Indians ... Provided, That the subdivisions upon which are located improvements to be appraised ... shall be offered to the highest bidder at public sale, after published notice of at least thirty days by the Secretary of the Interior, and the same shall be absolutely reserved from occupation or claim until so sold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proceeds first reimburse federal expenditures under the act, then pay for lands at $1.25/acre; improved lots to be publicly offered after 30 days' notice and are reserved from occupation until sale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-allotment civil/criminal status and tax/execution protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon the completion of said allotments and the patenting of the lands to said allottees, each and every of the said Indians shall be subject to the provisions of section nineteen hundred and seventy-seven of the Revised Statutes and to the laws, both civil and criminal, of the State or Territory in which they may reside, with the right to sue and be sued in the courts thereof: Provided, That their lands and personal property shall not be subject to taxation or execution upon the judgment, order, or decree of any court obtained on any cause of action which may arise during the period named in the above recited agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allottees gain access to state/territorial courts and are subject to laws, but their lands and personal property are protected from taxation and execution during the period specified in the agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treasury trust fund to yield $50,000 at 4% (alternate provision)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary of the Treasury shall, out of any moneys in the Treasury not otherwise appropriated, set apart, and hold as a perpetual trust-fund for said Ute Indians, an amount of money sufficient at four per centum to produce annually fifty thousand dollars, which interest shall be paid to them per capita in cash, annually, as provided in said agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treasury to establish a capital fund whose 4% interest yields $50,000/year for per-capita cash distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuation and discretionary distribution of certain salaries/awards
rubrics_metrics.description: All salaries paid to any member or members of the Ute tribe under existing treaty stipulations shall be continued for the term of ten years beyond the time fixed in said treaties. And the sum of four thousand dollars per annum for the term of ten years shall be distributed by the President at his discretion to such of said Indians as distinguish themselves by good sense, energy, and perseverance in the pursuits of civilized life ... and there is hereby appropriated ... four thousand dollars as the first installment for such purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Existing treaty salaries extended for ten years; $4,000/year appropriated for discretionary awards to deserving Indians for ten years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of Title 28 R.S. to allotments administration
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions of title twenty-eight of the Revised Statutes shall extend over and be applicable to every allotment of land provided for in the foregoing agreement, and to the administration of the affairs of said Indians, so far as said provisions can be made applicable thereto.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General administrative legal provisions (Title 28 R.S.) apply to allotments and administration where practicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reservation of hot springs and public dedication
rubrics_metrics.description: The hot springs located in what is known as 'The Uncompahgre Park' ... and four square miles of land surrounding said springs and within said valley, are hereby reserved, and withdrawn from settlement, occupancy, or sale, under the laws of the United States, and dedicated and set apart for the benefit and enjoyment of the people; and, so far as practicable, the provisions of sections twenty-four hundred and seventy-four and twenty-four hundred and seventy-five, of the Revised Statutes, are hereby made applicable to said tract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specified natural feature and surrounding 4-square-mile tract withdrawn from private disposition and dedicated for public benefit; certain R.S. provisions applied as practicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriations subject to ratification condition and certification
rubrics_metrics.description: For the purpose of carrying the provisions of this act into effect, the following sums ... are appropriated ... For the payment of the expenses of the commissioners ... $25,000. For the cost of removal and settlement ... $350,000. For the sum to be paid to said Ute Indians, per capita, ... $15,000. For the payment of the appraised value of individual improvements ... $20,000. For the care and support ... $12,000: Provided, That with the exception of the appropriation for expenses of the commissioners, the above appropriations shall become available only upon the ratification of said agreement by three-fourths of the male adult members of the Ute Indians as provided in this act, and the certification of such fact to the Secretary of the Treasury by the Secretary of the Interior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Major appropriations are contingent on the 3/4 adult-male ratification and official certification; commissioners' expenses are immediately available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agreement expiration if not ratified within four months
rubrics_metrics.description: If the agreement as amended in this act is not ratified by three-fourths of the adult male Indians of the Ute tribes within four months from the approval of this act the same shall cease to be of effect after that day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time-limited ratification window: 4 months after approval; failure voids the agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secretary to account for Osage land alienations and reimburse trust
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary of the Interior is hereby authorized and directed to cause an account to be stated of the number of acres of the Osage lands in the State of Kansas that have in any way been alienated ... and of the money received by the United States on account of the sales of such lands, and to certify the difference between the sum so received and the sum that would be due said trust ... That a sum of money equal to the amount certified ... is hereby appropriated ... after defraying the cost of survey and sale of said lands and other expenses ... the balance of said funds shall be placed in the Treasury of the United States, to the credit of said Indians, to be invested and distributed in accordance with existing treaties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secretary must compute acreage alienated and receipts, certify shortfall, and direct Treasury to place equivalent funds to the Indians' credit after reasonable costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification of substitute school lands to State of Kansas
rubrics_metrics.description: The lands so selected by the State of Kansas be, and the same are hereby, confirmed to said State; and the Secretary of the Interior be, and hereby is, authorized to certify the same to said State, in lieu of sections sixteen and thirty-six, sold and disposed of by the United States, within the limits of any former Indian reservation as aforesaid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selected substitute lands confirmed and to be certified in lieu of previously reserved school sections that were disposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority for private suits for wrongs and claims against the United States
rubrics_metrics.description: That Elias C. Boudinot ... be, and he is hereby, authorized to bring suit in the Court of Claims against the United States Government, to recover what may be due to him in justice and equity for the loss inflicted upon him by reason of said seizure ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Congress may authorize individual claimants to sue the United States in Court of Claims for specific wrongs arising from federal actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific appropriations and recoupment from Indian annuities for damages
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary of the Treasury ... authorized and directed to pay Henry Warren ... the sum of fifteen thousand eight hundred and sixty-seven dollars and fifty cents ... and that the Secretary of the Interior be ... directed to retain, out of any annuities due or to become due the Comanche and Kiowa Indians, the sum of eleven thousand eight hundred and fifty-two dollars and fifty cents, and from any annuities due or to become due the Cheyennes the sum of four thousand and fifteen dollars, and cover the same into the Treasury in accordance with treaty stipulations between said Indian tribes and the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Congress can appropriate funds for private claims and direct recoupment from tribal annuities consistent with treaty terms.
